messages:
andrew: FYI customer SkipWave opened a support ticket — they're seeing repeated 503s and billing spikes. looks like dedicated pool keeps scaling up then immediately down, every ~3m. attaching notes. :frowning:
ops-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool skipwave-prod autoscaler triggered scale_up -> scale_down x7 in last 25m. avg_cpu 62% -> 15% after scale down. incident:INC-4219
mira: can you paste the tenant id and timeframe? any correlating deploys or LB config changes? :eyes:
andrew: tenant=skipwave-prod-42. spikes from 2026-03-17T09:12 -> 09:40 UTC. no deploys. customer says traffic is bursty (short spikes, many concurrent small requests).
sam: quick glance at metrics: scaling metric is 95th-percentile latency over 60s window. spikes are 10–15s long, so the 60s window smooths but values drop below threshold after new nodes spin up -> autoscaler tears down. that's classic oscillation.
leo: any noisy-neighbor CPU steal on nodes after scale up? I remember a similar case where background batch jobs killed the headroom.
andrew: logs show evict events and ephemeral throttles right after scale up. also saw kernel OOM-killer on one instance (low prob but recorded). attaching snippet:
```
Mar 17 09:18:21 node-gpu-37 docker[1234]: evict: container skipwave-infer-12 killed for memory_pressure
Mar 17 09:18:22 node-gpu-37 kubelet: kubelet.eviction: memory.available < threshold
```
mira: ok so two signals: 1) autoscaler sensitive to short spikes (60s 95p) 2) backfill/noisy tenants causing contention after node comes up. propose: increase cooldown, change metric to a longer window or use burst detection, and add minimum replica floor and hysteresis.
sam: proposed quick mitigation (non-disruptive):
- bump cooldown from 120s -> 300s
- change metric window 60s -> 120s and switch from 95p -> 90p
- set min_replicas = current+1 for 30m for this pool
- enable soft-padding: allocate +1 GPU buffer for 15m during business hours
I can patch autoscaler flags and run a canary on skipwave-prod.
leo: +1 to padding. also add a check to ignore spikes < 8s when computing percentiles (helps with very short bursts).
andrew: can we also throttle tenant-side retry storms? customer uses aggressive client retries that amplify spikes. asked them to backoff while we stabilise.
mira: if we change cooldown, need ops approval (risk: slower reaction to real sustained load). schedule 15m window to test with controlled changes.
ops-bot: DEPLOY-CANDIDATE created: autoscaler/tune/skipwave-20260317. approvers: mira, ops-oncall.
sam: patch ready: diff:
```
- cool_down: 120
- metric_window: 60
- percentile: 95
+ cool_down: 300
+ metric_window: 120
+ percentile: 90
+ min_replicas_policy: temp_floor(current+1, duration=1800)
+ padding: +1 (15m)
```
leo: also adding a node prewarm hook so new gpus come up with cache warmed for frequent models (reduces latency post-scaleup).
andrew: customer agreed to pause retries for 30m. i'll monitor errors and billing. scheduling: patch at 09:55 UTC, monitor 09:55-10:25.
mira: i'll review after the 30m. if oscillation stops, we'll roll this to similar noisy pools and create runbook entries.
andrew: quick followups: create support ticket update, note to billing to freeze any suspicious overages while we triage.
sam: doing rollout now to canary pool skipwave-canary -> link: https://console.internal/redwood/ops/autoscaler/patch/skipwave-20260317
leo: ping me if kernel OOMs keep happening; need to isolate noisy tenants. might schedule tenant isolation for next maintenance.
andrew: thanks team. will close iff errors drop below 1% for 30m. :thumbsup:
